title: The conditional operator
recap: The conditional operator condition ? expression1 : expression2 evaluates its condition and then exactly one of its two alternatives. It is C++'s only ternary operator and is an expression, so its result can initialize a variable.

Conditional expressions are best kept simple. Parenthesizing the entire conditional often improves readability, and an if statement is preferable when either branch needs multiple statements or significant side effects.
objectives: Use a relational expression as a conditional operator condition.
Select both a numeric charge and a text label.
Store conditional results in appropriately typed const variables.
Rely on exactly one selected branch.
warnings: Do not confuse the colon in the conditional operator with a statement separator.
Both alternative expressions must have compatible types for the intended result.
Do not replace a clear multi-statement decision with nested conditional operators.
challenge: For a subtotal of 42 and a free-shipping threshold of 50, calculate whether the order qualifies. Use conditional operators to select a shipping charge of 0 or 7 and a std::string_view label of free or standard. Calculate and report the final total.
hints: Use the same condition to select string-view literals, then add shippingCharge to subtotal.
